THE STARTING POINT

What you can build from here.

A good starting point when…

Developers who already have application code and want an infrastructure-first azd foundation.

  • Terraform module structure and provider configuration.
  • azd application and infrastructure configuration.
  • Dev Container tooling setup.
  • GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines workflow assets.
Before choosing this template

This is a starter blueprint, not a complete running app. No default host or database is implied by the modules that the repository includes.

HOW THE PIECES CONNECT

Understand the shape of the solution.

Your app→azure.yaml→Terraform→Your Azure resources
CONCEPTUAL FLOW · NOT A VERIFIED DEPLOYMENT TOPOLOGY

Conceptual workflow, not a preconfigured application topology. Hosting, databases and application language depend on the code and infrastructure you add.

View the complete repository architecture ↗

BEFORE YOU START

Check your environment.

  • Terraform 1.1.7 or later, Azure CLI and Azure Developer CLI.
  • An Azure subscription; review the README's Azure CLI authentication and subscription configuration.
  • Your own application code and Terraform resource configuration before application deployment.

For every deployment: confirm your subscription, permissions, target region, model quota where applicable, and likely charges. Reading this page does not validate any of those.

Check the current setup instructions ↗

WHAT IS INCLUDED

Services and integrations.

Declared integrations can include optional resources or deployment variants. They are not a guarantee of default provisioning.

No application resources are assumed.

Add your own application and infrastructure configuration using the repository's starter modules.

FROM EVALUATION TO ACTION

Your next steps, in order.

  1. Review the template and its hooks.

    Inspect repository setup scripts, required permissions and deployment instructions before executing code.

  2. Initialize a new project.

    Use a new directory, then run the template's init command.

    azd init -t azd-starter-terraform
    Repository setup instructions ↗

  3. Review costs, then approve deployment.

    Follow the repository guide to authenticate, configure your environment and deploy. Cloud resources can incur charges even after an interrupted deployment. Nothing on this website runs azd up for you.

    Open the Azure pricing calculator ↗

  4. Clean up when you are finished.

    azd down deletes the resources created for an environment. Review the target environment and approve deletion before running it.
